clauses.clause: Para. 1: modifies the Paulina National Forest boundaries by eliminating the described Oregon lands
Para. 2 (first part): opens the excluded lands, subject to valid rights and existing withdrawals, to actual settlers only under the homestead laws from 9 a.m. May 9, 1914 through June 7, 1914
Para. 2 (second part): thereafter opens the lands to entry and disposition under any and all applicable public land laws

Para. 3 (first sentence): persons settling between the order date and 9 a.m. May 9, 1914, or on or occupying the lands at that hour, are considered and dealt with as trespassers and preference is given the prior legal applicant; examination of the lands is permitted
Para. 3 (last sentence): persons having prior settlement rights will be allowed to make entry in conformity with existing law and regulations

conclusion.basis_rule: none_established_for_whole_order (para. 1 spent_on_issue; settlers-only window expired under own terms; remaining commands open)

data_errors: shepard-citations lead EO:10454 -> EO:1899 is false: the FR contents line reads 'July 20, 1899 (see EO 10454)', an order identified by date; the parser took the year 1899 as an order number.

shepard-citations lead PLO:1140 -> EO:1899 'revoked in part' is false for the same reason: PLO 1140 partly revokes the Executive order of June 13, 1899 (Alaska), per the BLM PLO table. The quoted contents line also runs into '4131', which is EO No. 4131 of Jan. 22, 1925, the amending order.
Evidence slice 'president' field is empty; the held text is signed Woodrow Wilson.
OCR reads the opening date as 'the oth day of May, i914'; the next paragraph of the same text reads 'May 9, 1914', so the date is May 9, 1914.
The earlier T5 result depended on class doctrine PD-NATIONAL-FOREST, whose source S-ORGANIC (30 Stat. 11, 34-36) is not held; that reliance is withdrawn and recorded as gap g1.

gaps.missing: Whether the 'thereafter' opening to entry under the public land laws is a one-time restoration completed on June 8, 1914, or a continuing command; and whether any later instrument re-withdrew, re-reserved or otherwise disposed of the eliminated lands by naming this order.
gaps.where_it_would_be: The class doctrine source for national forest eliminations (PD-NATIONAL-FOREST / S-ORGANIC, 30 Stat. 11, 34-36, and the Act of September 30, 1913, 38 Stat. 113), neither held; later proclamations and orders on the Paulina, Deschutes and Fremont National Forests; BLM Oregon land status records for the listed townships.

gaps.clause: Para. 3 (first sentence), trespasser treatment and applicant preference
gaps.missing: Evidence that the trespasser-treatment and prior-legal-applicant-preference commands were exhausted (all affected claims adjudicated) or were ended by a later instrument naming the order. The order's text gives them no end date.
gaps.where_it_would_be: General Land Office local land-office adjudication records for the Oregon districts covering these townships (National Archives, Record Group 49), or a later Executive order, proclamation or public land order expressly disposing of them.

gaps.clause: Para. 3 (last sentence), entry by persons with prior settlement rights
gaps.missing: Evidence that all prior settlement rights on the eliminated lands were entered, relinquished or otherwise finally disposed of, or a later instrument ending the allowance.
gaps.where_it_would_be: Same land-office entry and adjudication records (Record Group 49) and BLM tract books for the listed townships.

moves.note: ProQuest replica of the State Department copy is held and was re-read in full; operative words legible; operative clauses listed.

Operative status is OPEN with named gaps. The boundary elimination is spent on issue and the settlers-only window expired by its own dates, but the order's text sets no end to the trespasser-treatment and applicant-preference command, to the prior-settler entry clause, or to the general opening, and no source ending them is held.

Every clause now has a state: two ended with a date and quotation from the order, three open with the gap named. This rests on reading 'open with the gap named' as an allowed clause state; if the coordinator reads T4 more strictly, the result is T3.

Three gaps remain (see gaps). The earlier T5 claim is withdrawn: it treated the May 9 cutoff that identifies affected settlers as an expiry of the consequences, and relied on class doctrine PD-NATIONAL-FOREST whose source is not held.

review.conclusion_reason: NO by June 8, 1914 is unsupported. Boundary elimination was performed and the exclusive settlement window expired, but no cited source ends or establishes completion of the applicant-preference and trespasser-treatment commands. Operative status should remain OPEN pending evidence addressing those commands, such as implementing land-office adjudication records or a later instrument expressly disposing of them. Formal status is supported only as no express ending found in the checked sources; both supplied later-instrument leads concern other orders. The submitted result contains no upheld whole-order status basis sufficient for T3.
missed_evidence: jobs/pinakes-proquest-ingest/output/texts/EO_1899.txt, final paragraph: 'or who are on or are occupying any part of such lands at said hour' extends the affected class beyond the truncated p7 quotation; 'will be considered and dealt with as trespassers and preference will be given the prior legal applicant' supplies no May 9 termination of those consequences.

Same file, final sentence: 'Persons having prior settlement rights, as above defined, will be allowed to make entry in conformity with existing law and regulations.' The result groups this with paragraph 3 but supplies no basis for its claimed May 9 ending.
review.suspected_defect: The p7 quotation truncates the sentence and converts a cutoff identifying affected conduct into an expiration of the resulting commands. The blanket spent-on-issue conclusion then treats that unsupported expiration as established. Intent cannot be determined.

verdicts.reason: Held original OCR confirms Wilson's signature, March 12, 1914, and No. 1899.
Paragraph 1 expressly modifies the boundary by eliminating the described lands.
Read with the operative sentence in p2, the boundary elimination is performed by the order itself; the opening sentence cites the 1897 Act.
The full paragraph expressly ends the settlers-only period on June 7, 1914, although the supplied excerpt omits that date.

The text confirms general entry thereafter, but does not establish that nothing further operated under the order. The scheduled opening does not itself prove exhaustion of the separate preference and treatment commands.
Paragraph 2 expressly preserves valid rights and existing withdrawals, explaining that those withdrawals should not now be revoked or modified.

May 9 bounds the settlement conduct and occupancy identifying affected persons, not the duration of their treatment as trespassers or applicant preference. The omitted continuation also covers persons occupying the lands at that hour.
The original expressly directs trespasser treatment and preference for the prior legal applicant, subject to its stated exceptions.
The held Federal Register text's codification guide identifies July 20, 1899, not Executive Order No. 1899.
EO 10454's opening recital confirms Hawaiian military lands reserved by the July 20, 1899 order.
The cited BLM PDF, page 14, entry 1140, confirms April 28, 1955, 20 FR 3027, Alaska, and partial revocation of the June 13, 1899 order as amended by EO 4131.
